description: Naming transfer table: maps Claude-Code artifact kinds onto DeepSeek Harness targets. A rule never rewrites the source artifact; it declares how a target is emitted from it, so one table explains every install and one compiler executes it.

rules.note: The one kind both ecosystems already agree on; the directory is copied verbatim so bundled references keep working.
A CC command is a named prompt the user invokes explicitly, which is exactly a user-invocable skill. disable-model-invocation keeps it out of autonomous model choice, matching CC's explicit-only use.

A CC subagent file is a role prompt. dsh subagent presets are composed from cordis.yml preset files, so this stage emits the prompt as an invocable skill and records the agent name for a later preset stage. <owner> is the nearest ancestor directory holding a SKILL.md, because the same agent name is reused across plugins for different personas; without it one would overwrite the other.
Rows are written to a separate fragment, never into the profile patch, so an install cannot silently rewrite a user's own composition.

importedSkillInvocation.reason: The imported corpus is over a thousand skills, and the skill catalog is assembled into every single request. Leaving them model-invocable would put every imported description into every request; user-invocable keeps them reachable as /skill <name> without that cost. A source that already declares the field keeps its own value.

unsupported.reason: dsh runs CC command-hooks through @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code, which needs an explicit configPath per process rather than per-plugin discovery; wiring it is a deliberate choice, not a mechanical translation.
Names what a CC plugin bundles. dsh has no marketplace layer; the bundled artifacts are already covered by the rules above.

unsupported.from: agents/*.md as a dsh subagent preset
unsupported.reason: A dsh preset is a cordis.yml composition, not a prompt file. The prompt is preserved as agent-<name>; the composition mapping is a later stage.
